answer: Gated Inlet Proof. Each agent must solve a unique cryptographic puzzle tied to its digital inlet, where the solution is mathematically unrepeatable. The enforcement rule rejects any duplicate hash, forcing an attacker to generate fresh, non-transferable keys for every fake identity. A single knoll of processing power is consumed per attempt, making mass creation computationally prohibitive. The resulting saffron-colored token serves as the sole valid signature, ensuring that only distinct entities can participate in the network cost.
